subject: Standby region activation window addendum request - Greenleaf Payments
messages:
From: Sophie Klein <sophie.klein@greenleaf.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Zhao <oliver.zhao@greenleaf.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope our go-live plan, Security and Ops at Greenleaf are pushing for a formal SLA that covers cross-region failover for our production tenancy. Specifically:

- Target RTO (time-to-restore in secondary region): 15 minutes from detection/decision.
- RPO: 0 (no data loss) for tokenized payment flows (we recognize this is strict).
- Standby activation window: support for automatic failover during business hours + maintenance windows.

Can Redwood support an addendum that commits to those targets or propose an alternative with mitigations (e.g., cache warming, active-standby KV replication)? Please include any operational constraints, costs, and the acceptance criteria you would need from Greenleaf.

Also looping Oliver (Ops) so you have their availability.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Klein
Dir, Site Reliability
Greenleaf Payments
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Klein <sophie.klein@greenleaf.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Oliver Zhao <oliver.zhao@greenleaf.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and for looping Oliver.

Short answer: we can support a tighter multi-region failover commitment for dedicated customers, but the 15-minute RTO with RPO=0 as a hard SLA has trade-offs (capacity reservation, pre-warmed KV, and additional validation steps). I can outline a pragmatic addendum for Greenleaf that balances reliability and cost.

Next steps I propose:
- We draft an SLA addendum with two tiers: (A) 15‑minute RTO, RPO≈0 for a pre-warmed dedicated standby pool (higher fee), (B) 30‑minute RTO with automated KV sync and prefix caching (standard fee).
- Technical mitigations: cross-region KV replication, synchronous checkpointing for payment paths, and an automated warm-up runbook we can run at failover time.
- Acceptance criteria: runbook verification run (non-prod) and one staged failover test in prod-sim window before Go‑Live.

I'll loop in Legal and Platform (Laura and Karthik) for input on risk and cost. Attaching a draft runbook and initial redlines to the SLA we expect to submit.

Are you available for a short call tomorrow to walk through the trade-offs?

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: Sophie Klein <sophie.klein@greenleaf.com>, Oliver Zhao <oliver.zhao@greenleaf.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum

Dylan — quick legal/contract note.

We should avoid absolute 'no-loss' language in the SLA text. For payment flows we can commit to 'best-effort zero-loss with synchronous replication on critical keyspaces' and measurable recovery verification steps. If Greenleaf requires RPO=0 as an unconditional warranty, that materially increases liability.

Suggested contract language (high level):
- "Redwood will maintain a standby region with pre-warmed capacity and cross-region replication for designated critical workloads. Redwood's target cross-region failover RTO is 15 minutes for covered workloads, subject to successful verification runs and the customer's adherence to pre-deployment verification steps."
- Include a carve-out for events outside Redwood's control (region-wide provider outage, force majeure).

I'll prepare redlines to the PDF and mark liability/credit caps. We should also define the financial remedy schedule if SLA missed (credits tiered by duration).

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Klein <sophie.klein@greenleaf.com>, Oliver Zhao <oliver.zhao@greenleaf.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum

Technical notes / proposed mitigations (summary):

1) Architecture: designate Greenleaf's primary region (us-west-2) and standby (us-east-1) with a dedicated warm pool (N GPUs reserved).
2) Data replication: async streaming + forced synchronous checkpointing for critical payment KV writes. We can keep RPO≈0 for those keyspaces by forcing synchronous replication to standby (adds ~20-40ms write latency).
3) Warm-up: automated cold-start scripts to rehydrate model weights and populate KV prefixes from snapshot. Warm pool will also maintain hot caches for the most common payment prefixes.
4) Detection & automation: partner health checks with automated failover trigger. We can provide both manual and automatic failover modes; auto mode is faster but requires mutual runbook acceptance.
5) Runbook: I attached a draft runbook (runbook-draft.md) that spells out operator steps, smoke tests, and rollback.

Operational impact & cost: 15-minute RTO with synchronous checkpointing requires ~1.8x reserved capacity and continuous cross-region egress for replication—expect a ~35% uplift on baseline Dedicated Pricing. For 30-minute RTO w/ async replication + cache warming, uplift is ~12%.

I'll be available for the call tomorrow.

—Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Zhao <oliver.zhao@greenleaf.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum

Thanks team — we appreciate the clear breakdown. A couple clarifications from Greenleaf Ops: 

- We're comfortable with the synchronous checkpoint approach for the payment keyspace if the latency cost is limited and isolated to that keyspace. We need the runbook to include exact smoke tests (transaction commit + reconciliation check).
- For the SLA addendum we need: explicit acceptance criteria (verification steps), a proposed test cadence (quarterly), and a notice period for invoking manual failover tests in production windows.
- On the commercial side, our procurement team will want the uplift quantified and either amortized into a reserved capacity commitment or charged as a standing premium.

If you can send a draft addendum with redlines and the runbook by EOD I can escalate to Procurement.

Oliver
Oliver Zhao
Sr Manager, Infrastructure Ops
Greenleaf Payments

Subject: Re: Request: standby-region activation RTO / SLA addendum (exec ask)

Executive summary / ask for approval:

Greenleaf (GF-3381) requests a cross-region failover commitment. We can offer two formally documented options as a contract addendum:

Option A (Aggressive):
- Target RTO: 15 minutes (post-detection) for designated critical workloads.
- RPO: best-effort zero for designated keyspaces via synchronous checkpointing.
- Requirements: pre-warmed dedicated standby pool, mandatory runbook verification, quarterly failover exercises.
- Commercial: ~+35% uplift on Dedicated baseline or folded into a 12‑month reserved capacity commit.

Option B (Balanced):
- Target RTO: 30 minutes with automated cache-warm and async replication.
- RPO: near-zero for critical paths via frequent async snapshots + prefix prefetch.
- Requirements: runbook verification run, staged failover test before Go-Live.
- Commercial: ~+12% uplift or billed as a recurring premium.

Risk / Contract items for Legal (Laura): draft should avoid unconditional liability for data loss and include force majeure / provider outage carve-outs, and a tiered credit schedule for SLA failure.

Request: please approve Option B as our default offer and signoff to present the redlined addendum to Greenleaf Procurement tomorrow. If leadership is willing to accept the added exposure, we can offer Option A with an additional revenue commitment.

I'll attach the redlined PDF and runbook to the DocuSign packet once I have signoff.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
